tutorials.title: Long-Tail Cast On
tutorials.summary: The most common way to start a knitting project.

steps.title: Leave a tail
steps.text: Pull out about one inch of yarn for every stitch you need, plus a few extra inches. Make a slip knot and place it on your needle.

steps.title: Hold the yarn
steps.text: Wrap the tail end around your left thumb and the working yarn around your left index finger. Hold both strands with your other fingers.

steps.title: Make the first stitch
steps.text: Bring the needle up through the loop on your thumb, catch the strand from your index finger, and pull it back through the thumb loop. Drop the thumb loop and tighten gently.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Keep going until you have the number of stitches your pattern asks for. Keep the tension even, not too tight.

tutorials.title: The Knit Stitch
tutorials.summary: Learn the basic knit (k) stitch, the foundation of garter stitch.

steps.title: Set up
steps.text: Hold the needle with the cast-on stitches in your left hand. Keep the working yarn behind the work.

steps.title: Insert
steps.text: Slide the right needle into the front of the first stitch on the left needle, from left to right.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: Wrap the yarn counterclockwise around the tip of the right needle.

steps.title: Pull through
steps.text: Pull the loop through the stitch with the right needle and let the old stitch slip off the left needle.

tutorials.title: The Purl Stitch
tutorials.summary: The purl (p) stitch is the reverse of knit and creates ribbing.

steps.title: Bring yarn forward
steps.text: Keep the yarn in front of the work.

steps.title: Insert
steps.text: Slide the right needle into the front of the next stitch from right to left.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: Wrap the yarn counterclockwise around the right needle, going over the top and then under.

steps.title: Pull through
steps.text: Draw the loop back through the stitch and slip the old stitch off the left needle.

tutorials.title: Basic Bind Off
tutorials.summary: Finish your knitting so the edge stays neat and does not unravel.

steps.title: Knit two
steps.text: Knit the first two stitches as normal.

steps.title: Pass over
steps.text: Insert the left needle into the first stitch you knitted and lift it over the second and off the needle.

steps.title: Knit one more
steps.text: Knit the next stitch so there is one stitch on the right needle again, then pass the previous one over it.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Repeat until one stitch is left. Cut the yarn, leave a tail, and pull it through the last loop.

tutorials.title: Magic Ring
tutorials.summary: Start amigurumi and flower projects with a tight, closed center.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: Wrap the yarn around two fingers, leaving a tail of about six inches.

steps.title: Insert
steps.text: Insert the hook into the ring, catch the working yarn, and pull up a loop.

steps.title: Chain
steps.text: Chain the number of stitches your pattern asks for (usually one or two).

steps.title: Close the ring
steps.text: Work your stitches into the ring, then pull the tail to close it tightly.

tutorials.title: Single Crochet (sc)
tutorials.summary: The shortest and densest basic stitch, great for amigurumi.

steps.title: Insert
steps.text: Insert the hook into the next stitch, under both loops of the top.

steps.title: Yarn over
steps.text: Yarn over and pull up a loop. You now have two loops on the hook.

steps.title: Yarn over again
steps.text: Yarn over one more time and pull through both loops.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: You have one single crochet. Move to the next stitch and repeat.

tutorials.title: Double Crochet (dc)
tutorials.summary: Taller and more open than sc, so projects grow faster.

steps.title: Yarn over
steps.text: Yarn over before you insert the hook into the stitch.

steps.title: Insert and pull up
steps.text: Insert the hook into the stitch and pull up a loop. You have three loops on the hook.

steps.title: Two at a time
steps.text: Yarn over and pull through two loops, then yarn over and pull through the last two.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Move to the next stitch and repeat the same steps.

tutorials.title: Making a Granny Square
tutorials.summary: Build a square with corners using clusters and chain spaces.

steps.title: Start the center
steps.text: Make a magic ring, ch 3, then work 2 dc into the ring. Ch 2, and work (3 dc, ch 2) three times into the ring.

steps.title: Join the round
steps.text: Slip stitch to the top of the first ch 3 to close the round.

steps.title: Work the corners
steps.text: Slip stitch into the next chain space. Ch 3, then (2 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in the same space to make a corner.

steps.title: Continue around
steps.text: Ch 1, then (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in each corner space. Slip stitch to finish.

stitches.name: Knit
stitches.meaning: Insert the needle front to back, wrap, and pull through.

stitches.name: Purl
stitches.meaning: Insert the needle back to front, wrap, and pull through.

stitches.name: Knit two together
stitches.meaning: Knit two stitches as one, which decreases by one.

stitches.name: Stockinette stitch
stitches.meaning: Knit one row, purl the next. Smooth on one side.

stitches.name: Chain
stitches.meaning: The base stitch. Yarn over and pull through the loop.

stitches.name: Slip stitch
stitches.meaning: The shortest stitch. Used for joining rounds and moving.

stitches.name: Single crochet
stitches.meaning: Insert, yarn over, pull up, yarn over, pull through both loops.

stitches.name: Double crochet
stitches.meaning: Yarn over first, then pull up and work two loops off, twice.

patterns.title: Crochet Flower
materials: Worsted or DK cotton in two colors

steps.label: Round 1
steps.text: Make a magic ring. Ch 2, work 12 dc into the ring, sl st to the top of the first ch 2 to join.

steps.label: Round 2
steps.text: *Sl st into the next dc, ch 4, skip 1 dc.* Repeat from * 5 more times to make 6 loops. Sl st to join.

steps.label: Round 3
steps.text: In each ch-4 loop work (sc, hdc, 2 dc, hdc, sc) to make six petals. Sl st into the base to finish.

steps.label: Finish
steps.text: Cut the yarn, pull it through the last loop, and weave in the ends.

patterns.credit: Drafted with AI help by the StitchBook team. Not yet test-made by a person. Check every stitch count before you start, and tell us if something is wrong.

patterns.title: Garter Stitch Scarf
patterns.gauge: About 18 sts and 36 rows = 4 in in garter stitch

steps.label: Cast on
steps.text: Cast on 30 stitches using the long-tail cast on.

steps.label: Body
steps.text: Knit every row until the scarf measures about 60 inches, or until your yarn is almost gone. Leave enough yarn for the bind off.

steps.label: Bind off
steps.text: Bind off loosely using the basic bind off.

steps.label: Finish
steps.text: Weave in all ends and block lightly.

patterns.title: Ribbed Knit Hat
materials: US 7 (4.5 mm) 16 in circular needle for ribbing
US 8 (5.0 mm) 16 in circular needle for the body
patterns.gauge: About 20 sts = 4 in in stockinette stitch on US 8

steps.label: Cast on
steps.text: Cast on 80 stitches on the US 7 needle, join in the round, and place a marker.

steps.label: Ribbing
steps.text: Work k2, p2 ribbing for 2.5 inches (about 20 rounds).

steps.label: Body
steps.text: Switch to the US 8 needle. Knit every round until the hat measures 6 inches from the cast-on edge.

steps.label: Crown 1
steps.text: *K8, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 2
steps.text: *K7, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 3
steps.text: *K6, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 4
steps.text: *K5, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 5
steps.text: *K4, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 6
steps.text: *K3, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 7
steps.text: *K2, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 8
steps.text: *K1, k2tog* around.

steps.label: Crown 9
steps.text: K2tog around.

steps.label: Finish
steps.text: Cut the yarn, leave an 8 inch tail, thread it through the last 8 stitches, and pull tight. Weave in the ends.

patterns.credit: Drafted with AI help by the StitchBook team. Not yet test-made by a person. Check every stitch count before you start, and tell us if something is wrong.

patterns.title: Simple Granny Square

steps.label: Round 1
steps.text: Magic ring, ch 3 (counts as dc), 2 dc, ch 2, (3 dc, ch 2) three times. Sl st to the top of the first ch 3.

steps.label: Round 2
steps.text: Sl st into the next ch-2 space. Ch 3, (2 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in the same space to make the first corner. *Ch 1, (3 dc, ch 2, 3 dc) in the next corner space.* Repeat from * two more times. Ch 1, sl st to the top of the first ch 3 to join. (4 corners)

steps.label: Finish
steps.text: Fasten off, weave in the ends, and join squares as needed.

patterns.title: Quilted Poinsettia Wall Hanging
materials: Burgundy 1/2 yd, cream 1/2 yd, green 1/2 yd, red 1/2 yd
Background 1 yd, backing 1 yd, batting 32 in square
Rotary cutter, self-healing mat and clear acrylic ruler
Sewing machine with a walking foot and a 90/14 jeans needle
Water-soluble marker and pin-and-string circle compass
patterns.credit: Designed by HugStitchLoom. Measurements were calculated and geometrically checked, but these designs have not yet been physically sewn. Check every measurement on your first make.

steps.label: Cut
steps.text: Cut 64 petal squares: 16 burgundy 6-in, 16 cream 5-in, 12 green 5-in, 12 red 4-in, 8 red 3-in. Cut background, batting and backing 32-in squares. Stack each size separately.

steps.label: Fold
steps.text: Fold each square into a prairie-point petal: fold diagonally, then fold the two acute corners up to meet the right-angle corner. Make a test petal first; the point should be crisp.

steps.label: Press
steps.text: Press every petal with a hot dry iron, no steam. Restack by ring: 16, 16, 12, 12 and 8.

steps.label: Sandwich
steps.text: Lay the backing right side down, batting centered, background right side up. Smooth from the center outward and pin or spray-baste every 6 in.

steps.label: Guide circles
steps.text: Find the center by folding the sandwich in quarters. Draw light guide circles of 19, 15, 11.5, 8 and 4.5 in.

steps.label: Ring 1
steps.text: Arrange 16 burgundy petals on the 19-in circle, tips out, bases on the line, about 3.7 in apart. Pin through all layers. If the last petal will not fit, re-space the whole ring.

steps.label: Stitch and vein
steps.text: Stitch each petal base 1/4 in from the edge, with backstitching at both ends. Add a center vein on each petal with 3.0 mm straight stitch in gold thread.

steps.label: Rings 2 to 5
steps.text: Ring 2: 16 cream 5-in petals on the 15-in circle. Ring 3: 12 green 5-in petals on the 11.5-in circle, offset between the cream petals. Ring 4: 12 red 4-in petals on the 8-in circle. Ring 5: 8 red 3-in petals on the 4.5-in circle. Check each gap so no petal sits on top of its neighbour.

steps.label: Quilt
steps.text: Quilt the exposed background with curved echo lines 1/2 in apart, or a simple stipple. Keep clear of the petal tips.

steps.label: Beads
steps.text: Sew about 18 red beads in a tight cluster in the center, with doubled thread through all layers. Knot every third bead and tug-test every bead.

steps.label: Trim and bind
steps.text: Trim to a 30-in circle, turning the mat rather than the quilt. Bind with about 105 in of 2.25-in bias: machine-stitch to the front, fold to the back and hand-stitch.

steps.label: Sleeve and hang
steps.text: Make a 28 × 4 in sleeve, center it on the back 2 in below the top edge and stitch the long edges. Slide a rod through and hang.

patterns.title: Quilted Christmas Tree Wall Hanging
materials: Green 1 yd, gold 1/4 yd, brown 1/4 yd for the trunk
Background 1-1/4 yd, backing 1-1/4 yd, batting 30 × 34 in
About 14 red and gold beads, 8 mm
Rotary cutter, self-healing mat and clear acrylic ruler
Sewing machine with a walking foot and a 90/14 jeans needle
Water-soluble marker and pin-and-string circle compass
patterns.credit: Designed by HugStitchLoom. Measurements were calculated and geometrically checked, but these designs have not yet been physically sewn. Check every measurement on your first make.

steps.label: Cut
steps.text: Cut 26 green petals: 8 at 7 in, 7 at 6 in, 6 at 5 in, 5 at 4.5 in. Cut 8 gold 2.5-in squares and one 5 × 7-in brown trunk. Cut background, batting and backing 30 × 34 in.

steps.label: Sandwich
steps.text: Lay the backing right side down, batting in the middle, background right side up. Smooth from the center out and pin-baste every 4 in.

steps.label: Quilt first
steps.text: With a walking foot, quilt a diagonal 2-in crosshatch over the whole background before any petals go on.

steps.label: Fold and press
steps.text: Fold all 26 green petals and the 8 gold mini petals. Make a test petal first; press with no steam and restack by size.

steps.label: Trunk
steps.text: Center the brown trunk with its base 2 in from the bottom edge and stitch 1/4 in from the edge. Its top will sit under row 1.

steps.label: Tiers
steps.text: Row 1: 8 petals on the 9-in base line, 3.25 in apart. Row 2: 7 petals on the 14-in line, 3 in apart. Row 3: 6 petals on the 18.5-in line, 2.75 in apart. Row 4: 5 petals on the 22.5-in line, 2.5 in apart. Petal tips point down. Measure from both side edges.

steps.label: Stitch and vein
steps.text: Stitch every petal base and add a center vein with 3.0 mm straight stitch.

steps.label: Star topper
steps.text: Arrange the 8 gold mini petals in a starburst about 5 in across, centered 28 in from the bottom. Stitch the bases and sew one gold bead in the center.

steps.label: Ornaments
steps.text: Hand-sew about 14 red and gold beads across the tiers, in the middle third of each petal. Knot every third bead and tug-test every bead.

steps.label: Bind and hang
steps.text: Join 2.25-in strips into a strip of about 140 in. Machine-stitch to the front, fold to the back and hand-stitch. Add a hanging sleeve 2 in below the top edge and slide a rod through.

patterns.title: Quilted Holiday Wreath Wall Hanging
materials: Green 3/4 yd, red 1/4 yd for the bow
Background 3/4 yd, backing 3/4 yd, batting 24-in squares
Rotary cutter, self-healing mat and clear acrylic ruler
Sewing machine with a walking foot and a 90/14 jeans needle
Water-soluble marker and pin-and-string circle compass
patterns.credit: Designed by HugStitchLoom. Measurements were calculated and geometrically checked, but these designs have not yet been physically sewn. Check every measurement on your first make.

steps.label: Cut
steps.text: Cut 26 green 5-in squares. Cut the bow: 2 red loops at 10 × 7 in, 2 red tails at 4 × 10 in, and one 3 × 3-in red center. Cut background, batting and backing 24-in squares.

steps.label: Fold and press
steps.text: Fold all 26 green petals. Make a test petal first. Press with no steam and stack them in one pile.

steps.label: Sandwich and quilt
steps.text: Lay the backing right side down, batting, then background right side up. Quilt radiating straight lines from the center to the edge. Trim only after quilting, because quilting shrinks the sandwich by about 1/2 in.

steps.label: Guide circle
steps.text: Trim the quilted sandwich to a 22-in circle. Mark a 20-in leaf guide with the compass.

steps.label: Marker petals
steps.text: Place 4 petals first, tips out, at 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock on the guide. Spacing drift ruins a wreath, so these markers keep each quarter even.

steps.label: Fill the wreath
steps.text: Fill each quarter with 5 to 6 petals, 26 in total, tips out, about 2.4 in apart with about 1/2 in overlap. Pin each petal through all layers.

steps.label: Stitch and vein
steps.text: Stitch every petal base 1/4 in from the edge, working around the circle in order. Add a 3.0 mm green vein to each leaf.

steps.label: Berries
steps.text: Hand-sew about 22 red beads in clusters of three, in 7 or 8 clusters tucked where the leaves meet. Use doubled thread through all layers.

steps.label: Bow
steps.text: Fold each 10 × 7-in loop into a loop with raw edges to the center back and stitch. Layer the loops, add the tails behind, wrap the 3-in center square around the middle and stitch the bow to the top of the wreath through all layers.

steps.label: Bind
steps.text: Trim the check to 22 in and bind with about 75 in of 2.25-in bias, easing around the curve. Hand-stitch to the back.

steps.label: Sleeve and hang
steps.text: Add a hanging sleeve 2 in below the top edge and slide a rod through.

patterns.title: Quilted Snowflake Wall Hanging
materials: Background 3/4 yd, backing 3/4 yd, batting 20-in squares
Rotary cutter, self-healing mat and clear acrylic ruler
Sewing machine with a walking foot and a 90/14 jeans needle
Water-soluble marker and pin-and-string circle compass
patterns.credit: Designed by HugStitchLoom. Measurements were calculated and geometrically checked, but these designs have not yet been physically sewn. Check every measurement on your first make.

steps.label: Cut
steps.text: Cut 6 ice-blue 7-in squares and 12 white 4-in squares. Cut background, batting and backing 20-in squares.

steps.label: Fold and press
steps.text: Fold all 18 petals. Make a test petal first. Press with no steam and keep the blues and whites in separate piles.

steps.label: Sandwich and quilt
steps.text: Lay the backing right side down, batting, then background right side up. Quilt echo circles 1 in apart.

steps.label: Guides
steps.text: Trim to an 18-in circle. Mark a 16-in guide for the arms and a 12-in guide for the branches with the compass.

steps.label: Arms
steps.text: Place all 6 blue petals on the 16-in guide at 12, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 o'clock, tips out. Place all six before stitching any, because six-fold symmetry shows every error.

steps.label: Stitch and vein arms
steps.text: Pin each arm, stitch its base 1/4 in from the edge and add a 3.0 mm vein in silver or pale-blue thread.

steps.label: Branches
steps.text: Arrange the 12 white petals on the 12-in guide at the 30° marks, offset 15° from the blue arms, so each arm sits between two white petals. Stitch and vein each one.

steps.label: Crystal center
steps.text: Hand-sew about 12 crystal beads in a tight cluster in the center, with doubled thread through all layers twice per bead. Tug-test every bead.

steps.label: Trim and bind
steps.text: Trim the check to an 18-in circle and bind with about 62 in of 2.25-in bias, easing around the curve.

steps.label: Sleeve and hang
steps.text: Add a hanging sleeve 2 in below the top edge and slide a rod through.

patterns.title: Quilted Christmas Star Wall Hanging
materials: Background 3/4 yd, backing 3/4 yd, batting 22-in squares
Rotary cutter, self-healing mat and clear acrylic ruler
Sewing machine with a walking foot and a 90/14 jeans needle
Water-soluble marker and pin-and-string circle compass
patterns.credit: Designed by HugStitchLoom. Measurements were calculated and geometrically checked, but these designs have not yet been physically sewn. Check every measurement on your first make.

steps.label: Cut
steps.text: Cut 8 burgundy 6-in squares and 8 gold 4.5-in squares. Cut background, batting and backing 22-in squares.

steps.label: Fold and press
steps.text: Fold all 16 petals: 8 large burgundy, 8 smaller gold. Make a test petal first. Press with no steam and keep the colors separate.

steps.label: Sandwich and quilt
steps.text: Lay the backing right side down, batting, then background right side up. Quilt a simple diagonal grid across it.

steps.label: Guides
steps.text: Trim to a 20-in circle. Mark an 18-in guide and an 11-in guide, plus 8 tick marks on the inner circle halfway between the outer marks. Mark the offset ticks now; eyeballing the 22.5° offset later makes the star crooked.

steps.label: Back layer
steps.text: Arrange the 8 burgundy petals on the 18-in guide, tips out, about 7.1 in apart.

steps.label: Stitch back layer
steps.text: Pin with 2 pins each, stitch the bases 1/4 in from the edge and add 3.0 mm gold veins.

steps.label: Front layer
steps.text: Arrange the 8 gold petals on the 11-in guide, on the offset ticks, overlapping the burgundy bases. Stitch and vein each one.

steps.label: Bead center
steps.text: Hand-sew about 14 gold beads in a tight cluster in the center, with doubled thread through all layers twice per bead. Tug-test every bead.

steps.label: Trim and bind
steps.text: Trim the check to 20 in and bind with about 69 in of 2.25-in bias, easing around the curve.

steps.label: Sleeve and hang
steps.text: Add a hanging sleeve 2 in below the top edge and slide a rod through.
